hosting.comment: cleanUrls serves control.html at /control. Nothing emulates this locally except the Firebase emulator — `python3 -m http.server` returns 404 for the extensionless routes — so use `firebase emulators:start --only hosting` for local dev.

headers.comment: Filenames here are not content-hashed, so Firebase's default max-age=3600 serves a stale driver station for an hour after a deploy. Revalidate every time instead: these files are a few KB and the panel must never be a version behind the firmware.
The robot library and starter template are uploaded to hardware verbatim. A cached stale minibot.py would be written to a robot and then be very hard to explain, so these revalidate too.

cleanUrls means the pages are actually served at extensionless paths, which the *.html glob above does NOT match — verified in the emulator: /control came back with no Cache-Control at all, so Firebase's default max-age=3600 would apply and serve a stale driver station for an hour after a deploy. Same argument as the glob, so the same treatment. One entry per route: Hosting globs match path segments, and there is no extension left to match on.
